rows.core: Cult of Skaro must attack to roll one of four attack-trigger modes—artifact-team counters, draw two, Dalek token, or every-opponent life loss—and protects/multiplies repeated attacks.
rows.positive: Darkwater Catacombs can convert an existing mana into blue and black, assisting castability of Cyberman/copy protection spells under imperfect lands.
rows.cut_cost: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth passively lets every land tap for black in addition to original types, improving black access without an extra filter input while threatening some symmetric benefit to opponents.
rules: Cult of Skaro's attack trigger chooses a random mode when the trigger resolves; it is not a spell with a chosen X value.
Catacombs requires another paid mana for its filter ability and does not produce extra total mana from a sole land.
Urborg gives all lands the Swamp land type in addition to other types and therefore black mana abilities under normal rules.
Neither a filter land nor Urborg multiplies artifact creature counters, creates Daleks or advances extra combats directly.
Removing Urborg may alter black-pip availability for artifact protection or recurring attack engines; filtering can be superior only if real colored sources bottleneck.
rows.adverse: The proposed filter land introduces an input payment and loses Urborg's unconditional black fixing; the change is a mana-base hypothesis, not proof of improved commander-native attack triggers.
rows.followup: Compare exact payability for Cult of Skaro and three attack-support spells across source opening hands with Urborg vs Catacombs and opponent land benefits.

rows.core: Loki creates a tapped-attacking nonlegendary copy of another Villain, then rewards combat damage by Villains with draws; copied ETB/static/combat-damage abilities—not automatic attack triggers—matter.
rows.positive: Kid Loki is a one-blue Villain whose +1/+1-counter hexproof protection can sometimes shelter freshly countered Villains, and his second-card draw trigger grows him.
rows.cut_cost: Deflecting Swat is conditional free instant stack interaction with a commander controlled, redirecting threatening spell/ability targets at the key attack-copy or theft response window.
rules: Kid Loki is a one-mana Legendary God Hero Villain and therefore qualifies as an original legal other Villain for Loki's attack copying.
A tapped-and-attacking Kid Loki token does not produce an attack trigger just by entering the battlefield; it may contribute to Villain combat-damage draw.
The copy does not inherit +1/+1 counters on the original Kid Loki; it enters without copied counters unless another effect puts them on it.
Kid Loki grants hexproof to your creatures on which you placed a +1/+1 counter this turn; the protection is conditional and not universal.
Deflecting Swat's alternate free-cast condition requires controlling a commander and can redirect a targeted opponent interaction that would interrupt Loki.
rows.adverse: Kid Loki's potential protection depends on counters this turn and the other Vilain board, while losing a free redirection spell can expose the very attack-copy engine it supports.
rows.followup: Sequence second-card draws, counter placement, Loki copied Kid Loki and opponent targeted removal versus protected Deflecting Swat windows.

rows.core: Anhelo grants casualty 2 on each turn's first instant or sorcery spell; a power-2+ disposable creature at cast time is mandatory to get the spell copy.
rows.positive: Resonating Lute grants lands an additional tap ability to make two same-color mana restricted to casting instants/sorceries, enabling expensive copied spells while holding responses on opponents' turns.
rows.cut_cost: Black Market Connections produces life-costed card draw, Treasures and 3/2 changeling creature fodder each precombat main, supplying both casualty-eligible bodies and spells for Anhelo.
rules: Anhelo grants casualty only to first instant or sorcery spell you cast each turn, not each spell copied; sacrificing a power-2+ creature is an extra casting cost.
Resonating Lute grants lands a restricted mana ability, and this mana can be spent only on instant/sorcery SPELLS, not Anhelo himself or creature fodder.
Lute has a separate tap-draw activated ability requiring seven or more cards in hand at activation.
Black Market Connections' 3/2 shapeshifter meets casualty 2's power requirement, independently of creature type.
Replacing repeatable 3/2 bodies with mana acceleration may strand casualty spells without legal fodder.
rows.adverse: Lute may supercharge casting once assembled, but costs four mana and deletes a perpetual casualty body/treasure/draw source central to Anhelo's creature-spell exchange identity; source recorded raw-SHA mismatch remains flagged.
rows.followup: Run paired source-paid Anhelo casualty first-spell turns including available power-2+ fodder, Lute four-mana deployment and seven-card hand draw eligibility; preserve logical hash despite historical raw mismatch.

rows.core: Bjorna's artifact-sacrifice tap goads creatures while Cecily rewards attacking with an eleven-plus hand to cast an instant/sorcery from hand for free; Lutri is a distinct project-authorized companion.
rows.positive: Resonating Lute doubles land-provided mana for paid instants and sorceries and can draw while seven-plus cards remain in hand, potentially supporting Cecily's big-hand threshold.
rows.cut_cost: Talisman of Indulgence is cheap color fixing that helps cast and protect two commanders and permanent card engines; Lute's restricted mana cannot pay those non-instant/sorcery spells.
rules: Both Bjorna and Cecily are commanders through Friends forever and occupy two card slots of the 100-card deck.
Cecily's free cast requires eleven or more cards after her attack trigger's draw/life loss; the spell must be an instant or sorcery from hand.
Lute's granted land mana can only cast instant or sorcery spells; it cannot be spent on Cecily, Bjorna or activated abilities.
Lutri, the Spellchaser is an official Commander-banned card used as a companion only by explicit project exception; it is not a third commander or a sanctioned official legal companion.
Trade Secrets and Yawgmoth's Bargain remain separately approved project exceptions and cannot be described as officially Commander-legal.
rows.adverse: The mana-doubling spell engine has genuine Cecily payoff, but a four-mana setup replacing two-mana unconditional fixing can delay the eleven-card combat and protection, especially while its mana restriction doesn't cast commanders.
rows.followup: Evaluate two-commander costed opening hands and eleven-card attack turns with Lute versus Talisman, separately list the three project bans and correctly count Lutri outside the 100.

rows.core: Ashad grants casualty 2 to the first nonlegendary artifact spell each turn and gains +1/+1 counters whenever another creature you control is sacrificed; cheap artifact creatures and flash artifacts are protected.
rows.positive: Darkwater Catacombs filters blue/black mana from an existing source, potentially smoothing castability of the Grixis artifact/casualty setup.
rows.cut_cost: Great Furnace is an untapped artifact land that pays red, can be sacrificed to artifact effects and raises artifact count; unlike a spell, it is not itself a casualty-copy target.
rules: Ashad's casualty 2 applies to the first nonlegendary artifact SPELL you cast each turn; merely playing an artifact land is not casting an artifact spell.
Great Furnace is a land and artifact on battlefield and can feed artifact-sacrifice outlets or affinity/metalcraft counts.
Darkwater Catacombs is a nonartifact land and cannot contribute to artifact-permanent count, reducing the supporting resource base.
Catacombs' filter ability needs an extra paid mana before producing U/B, whereas Great Furnace directly taps for red.
Sacrificing a power-2+ creature for Ashad casualty both copies an eligible artifact spell and places a +1/+1 counter on Ashad through his separate triggered ability.
rows.adverse: The replacement cuts a cheap artifact permanent and self-sufficient red source for a filter land, potentially harming artifact thresholds and cheap sacrifice/copy engines.
rows.followup: Compare source-bound artifacts-on-battlefield, casualty activations and colored mana across first four turns including Great Furnace artifact sacrifice availability.
